counterfactual_missing_items: Deeply inverted T-waves in leads V2 to V4
T-waves became upright in V2 to V4
Inverted U-waves in leads V2 to V5
decisive_items: Total occlusion at the ostium of the left anterior descending coronary artery
response.rationale: R5 combines the classic exertional chest pain with the definitive angiographic total LAD occlusion, directly supporting an acute coronary syndrome. R6 also cites the occlusion and T-wave inversion but its label is broader (CAD) and lacks the symptom context.

rejected.why: Hypertension and elevated BP are risk factors, not the primary diagnosis given the total LAD occlusion.
Variant angina typically shows ST elevation during pain; here T-waves become upright and there is no ST elevation, and pain is exertional, not at rest.
Only cites the occlusion without the symptom or ECG changes, making it less complete than R5 or R6.
